claims.text: Nanostructured Pt alloyed with a transition metal such as Ni or Co can enhance catalytic activity for both HER and HOR relative to nanostructured pure Pt.
Nanostructured Pt alloyed with Ni or Co can have greater durability during HER and HOR than nanostructured pure Pt.
Alloying Pt with Ni or Co modifies the electronic structure of Pt.
Pt-transition-metal alloying produces atomic-scale alloy formation.
Atomic-scale Pt-transition-metal alloy formation can produce a modified Pt surface such as a Pt-skin.
Pt-transition-metal alloy formation adjusts the Pt d-band center.
The alloy-induced electronic modification optimizes hydrogen adsorption energy on Pt.
Optimized hydrogen adsorption energy facilitates faster HER and HOR kinetics.
The alloy-induced electronic modification improves catalyst stability.
Pt-transition-metal alloys are predicted to require lower overpotentials than pure Pt under identical acidic operating conditions.
Pt-transition-metal alloys are predicted to exhibit improved Tafel slopes relative to pure Pt under identical acidic operating conditions.
Pt-transition-metal alloys are predicted to maintain operation longer than pure Pt under identical acidic operating conditions.
The proposed enhancement may be limited to acidic media and moderate operating temperatures.
The activity and durability trend may not persist in alkaline media or at higher temperatures.
